newsitem.title: GERMANY: High soymeal price discourages EU imports - Toepfer.
newsitem.headline: High soymeal price discourages EU imports - Toepfer.

text.p: German trader Alfred C Toepfer said European Union imports of protein feeds dropped sharply following high soymeal prices in 1996 and so far no change was in sight.
EU protein feeds imports dropped by 2.2 million tonnes to 26.1 million tonnes in 1996 as soymeal imports within the total declined to 11.5 million from 12.8 million a year earlier.
However, imports of most other protein feeds rose slightly in 1996 over 1995 and corngluten feed looked set to recapture lost market share in 1997.
Toepfer said while EU grain prices had been falling since the 1996 harvest, soymeal had stayed up, underpinned in particular by dynamic Asian soymeal demand.
The EU compound feed industry had responded by including a higher share of grain in its mixes.
Global soymeal stocks were set to fall until the arrival of Latin American crops and oilmeals supplies in general were expected to barely cover demand in 1996/97, Toepfer said.
Livestock industries in Asia were expanding fast in response to growing meat demand.
This brought higher soymeal imports in China, Indonesia, Thailand, Malaysia, Pakistan, Vietnam and the Philippines, diverting volumes away from the EU.
But cornglutenfeed imports in the EU might rise to six milllion in 1997 from 5.2 million last year.
Processing of maize (corn) into alcohol and starch had been discouraged amid high prices in the U.S., the main suppler, but prices were now falling, Toepfer said.
